OTHER DISEASES: Not answered. FINAL DIAGNOSIS: PART 1: THYROID, TOTAL THYROIDECTOMY (45 GRAMS) -. A. PAPILLARY THYROID CARCINOMA, TWO FOCI, LEFI AND.RIGHT. B. LARGEST FOCUS: RIGHT (3.0 CM), WELL DEMARCATED, FOLLICULAR PATTERN PREDOMINANT (see. comment). C. LEFT FOCUS: TALL CELL VARIANT (0.8 CM). D. ALL FOCI CONFINED TO THYROID; NO ANGIOLYMPHATIC INVASION. E. ONE REACTIVE LYMPH NODE, NO TUMOR PRESENT (0/1). F. PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT2 NO. G. CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC THYROIDITIS. PART 2: LYMPH NODES, CENTRAL COMPARTMENT, SELECTIVE DISSECTION -. THREE LYMPH NODES, NO TUMOR PRESENT (0/3). COMMENT: Select slides were reviewed with Dr. who agree that the larger nodule contains. papillary carcinoma. Given the focality of the diagnostic nuclear features in the larger nodule, it is possible that the. carcinoma is arising within a follicular adenoma.
